title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
hints: a window is 'valid' (achievable with at most k replacements) exactly when window length minus the count of its most common letter is at most k. what does that tell you about when to grow vs shrink the window?
grow the window by moving the right edge forward, updating letter counts as you go
if the window ever becomes invalid (length - most-frequent-count > k), shrink from the left by one, updating counts
track the max window length seen - it never needs to shrink below its previous best, so you don't need to recheck validity after every single shrink
commonMistakes: recomputing the most-frequent-letter count from scratch for every window instead of maintaining it incrementally
shrinking the window more than necessary, or shrinking when the window is still valid
forgetting that the 'most frequent count so far' doesn't need to be perfectly accurate after shrinks, since it only ever needs to be a safe upper bound for tracking the max length

content.problemStatement:
You're given a string of uppercase letters and a number `k`. You may
change up to `k` characters in the string to any other uppercase
letter.

**Return the length of the longest substring you can make consist of a
single repeated letter after doing so.**
constraints: s consists of only uppercase English letters
notes: k = 0 (no replacements allowed, answer is the longest existing run)
k is large enough to replace almost the whole string
the string already consists of a single repeated letter

change one letter to turn a 4-letter stretch into a single repeated letter

optimal.pattern: variable-size sliding window, tracking the count of the most frequent letter currently in the window

bruteForce.approach: for every substring, count the most frequent letter in it and check if (length - that count) <= k, tracking the longest valid one
bruteForce.time: O(n^2) or O(n^3) depending on how the frequency count is recomputed
